A milestone in our quantum journey. We’re delivering our Majorana-2 tech to DARPA for on-site testing and evaluation at our new research center in Maryland.


[Gov. Wes Moore](https://www.linkedin.com/in/iamwesmoore?trk=public_post_reshare_feed-actor-name)


1d


Quantum has the potential to transform every part of our economy and society. By opening this new discovery center and partnering with Microsoft, we’re taking another step toward leading the nation in this emerging sector. Together, we’ll solve some of the world’s most pressing challenges – right here in Maryland.

Handing Majorana-2 to DARPA for on-site testing is the right kind of milestone — real evaluation outside the lab, not another roadmap slide. Pairing that with the new Maryland research center makes the Capital of Quantum story feel concrete.


[Abdul Ali T P](https://in.linkedin.com/in/abdul-ali-t-p-112055271?trk=public_post_comment_actor-name) 10h


Moving Majorana-2 out of the lab and into DARPA's hands for real-world evaluation is a huge signal — topological qubits have been more theoretical promise than practical reality for years. This is the kind of milestone that separates genuine breakthroughs from incremental progress. Exciting to watch


[Anjli Amin](https://uk.linkedin.com/in/anjli-amin-6b86b425?trk=public_post_comment_actor-name) 18h


The quantum milestone finance should watch is not the qubit count, it is the migration. Every card, bank ledger and stablecoin runs on cryptography with a shelf life, and swapping it out across thousands of counterparties is a decade of unglamorous work that has to start before the machine works, not after.


[Bhaskar Gangipamula](https://www.linkedin.com/in/bhaskargangi?trk=public_post_comment_actor-name) 9h


Handing the hardware to DARPA to load and run on their own terms says a lot. Keeping the testing in house would be easier. Opening it up for an outside team to check independently is a willingness to be held to the work, and that travels well beyond quantum.


[Amin Mojaveri](https://ir.linkedin.com/in/amin-mojaveri-aa3362271?trk=public_post_comment_actor-name) 15h


The "when people talk about quantum computing, they often focus on discrete technologies or individual milestones. But the future of quantum will depend on our ability to build the expertise, partnerships, and infrastructure needed to put those advances to work" is the line that matters. The Majorana 2 topological qubits going to DARPA for on-site testing is the concrete milestone. The public-private collaboration with Maryland and the university partnerships is the infrastructure layer. Good to see the ecosystem-over-milestone framing.
